evidence_items.explanation: The survey conducted February 22–March 5 reported regular organizational generative-AI use at 65%, nearly double its earlier survey. This is material counterevidence to a broad stagnation reading, but increased use does not establish that commercialization proceeded without reliability-related delays.

evidence_items.locator: Opening description of survey; findings under the subsequent deployment, risk, and experimentation sections
evidence_items.explanation: In this May–June survey, 68% reported moving no more than 30% of experiments into production, while 67% were increasing investment because of value already obtained. Compliance, risk management, governance and data problems featured among the barriers; the report does not isolate factual unreliability as their principal cause.

unresolved_gaps: No market-wide measure establishes how halting commercial progress was during the claimed period.
The strongest direct accuracy evidence concerns information services, rather than the entire generative-AI market.
The surveys do not establish how much commercial delay reliability caused relative to costs, integration, skills, data and governance.
Regular use, production deployment and commercial success are different measures.
